object.name: evi.gigaverb~
object.digest: Classic gigaverb reverb algorithm, mono in / stereo out, fdn / allpass
object.description: A mono-in, stereo-out reverb implementation by Juhana Sadeharju. Originally Max/MSP-ified by Olaf Matthes (2004) Version 1.0test5, (c) 1999-2006 Juhana Sadeharju / Olaf Matthes. Originally Gen-ified by Graham Wakefield (2011). 64-bit MSP reference version by Volker Böhm (2016). This evieve version with updated filtering and parameter smooting.
object.discussion: Note, in this evieve version there are slight differences in sound from the various Max versions, but this version is closer to the original (Sadeharju) and with slightly more diffuseness in the early taps and low-mid. Attribute descriptions in this documentation are mainly from the Olaf Matthes originals. For more information about other reverbs in evieve, see the 'evieve reverb' tab of the helpfile.

inlets.digest: Audio In Mono or Left or 1 / messages to evi.gigaverb~
inlets.description: Mono, Left or 1 depends on the 'stereo' attribute.

inlets.digest: Audio In Nothing or Right or 2 / messages to evi.gigaverb~
inlets.description: Nothing, Right or 2 depends on the 'stereo' attribute.

messages.name: pattrstorage
messages.digest: In left inlet, pattrstorage messages to evi.gigaverb~
messages.description: Prepending the word 'pattrstorage' allows you to send any message pattrstorage understands to the internal pattrstorage object - you can recieve pattrstorage output via the far right outlet.

attributes.name: bandwidth
attributes.description: 'This is like a damping control for the input, it has a similar effect to the damping control, but is subtly different.'

attributes.name: bypass
attributes.description: 'Bypass, signal unaffected when set to 1. Can be used to compare reverb signal with original signal and to save CPU power when gigaverb~ is not used.'

attributes.name: damping
attributes.digest: Normalised 0..1, lowpass if 1, bypass if 0, shelving in between
attributes.description: 'This controls the high frequency damping (a lowpass filter), values near 0 will make it sound very bright, values near 1 will make it sound very dark.'

attributes.name: early
attributes.description: 'The quantity of early reflections (scatter reflections directly from the source). Think of Lexicon's ambiance patches.'

attributes.name: highfrequency
attributes.description: High frequency point in Hz of the end of wet chain onepole shelving filters.

attributes.name: highgain
attributes.description: ± gain of the high shelving onpole filters. Negative values damp, positive values boost. -1..1 equates to approximately -10..10 dB.

attributes.name: late
attributes.description: 'The level of the classic reverb tail reflections.'

attributes.name: lowfrequency
attributes.description: Low frequency point in Hz of the end of wet chain onepole shelving filters.

attributes.name: lowgain
attributes.description: ± gain of the low shelving onpole filters. Negative values damp, positive values boost. -1..1 equates to approximately -10..10 dB.

attributes.name: reverb
attributes.description: 'Reverb decay time, in seconds. 7 is a good place to start. 0.1..360 seconds'

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: 'The size of the room, in meters. Excessively large, and excessively small values will make it sound a bit unrealistic. Values of around 30 sound good.'

attributes.name: smoothtime
attributes.description: Set the smoothing time in ms of all the internal parameter smoothing functions.

attributes.name: spread
attributes.description: Stereo spread (or 'width'), offsets L/R levels. Note, in Juhana Sadeharju and Graham Wakefield verions this is not available (fixed). In Olaf Matthes version this is object creation argument only. In evieve this can be modified in realtime at any time.

attributes.name: stereo
attributes.description: This is essentially a mono-in stereo-out reverb, but you can toggle 'stereo' 'on' ('1') to explicitly control L/R signals into the late diffusion section (and dry L/R). Default '0' 'off' (mono-in, stereo-out).
